answer: A trusted mesa node timestamps each agent registration into a copper-anchored ledger, so every new identity must burn a hardware-attested key whose issuance cost propagates as a ripple across the reputation graph. Colluding agents that spawn phantom identities therefore deplete bonded stake faster than they can recoup it, since each sybil link is scored against the shared. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
